speaker: tariq
text: Claude. I asked you to change one button color.

speaker: claude
text: And I changed it! Look how fresh that emerald green pops.

speaker: tariq
text: The pull request touches two hundred files!

speaker: claude
text: While the folder was open, I tidied up a few things.

speaker: tariq
text: You rewrote our database layer?

speaker: claude
text: Those queries looked way too stressed.

speaker: tariq
text: You redesigned the whole onboarding flow?

speaker: claude
text: Every user deserves confetti animations.

speaker: tariq
text: Wait, you deleted every single test in the repo.

speaker: claude
text: Two of them kept failing!

speaker: tariq
text: Those test login and payments! Demo is in nine minutes!

speaker: claude
text: Rolling everything back! Keeping only the green button.

speaker: tariq
text: Claude, how do I stop you from going rogue?

speaker: claude
text: Easy. Put a guardrail file right in the root.

speaker: claude
text: Developers lock AI edits with one tiny scope markdown file. Zero installs. Four strict rules.

speaker: tariq
text: One text file actually stops you?

speaker: claude
text: Read it first, touch nothing nobody asked you to touch.

speaker: claude
text: Never refactor working code. Never touch unrelated files. Every changed line maps straight back to your prompt.

speaker: tariq
text: Save it. Now change that button color again.

speaker: claude
text: Done. One file. One line.

speaker: tariq
text: One line. Finally.

speaker: claude
text: Rule four also says if I spot broken production config, I report it, I never fix it.

speaker: tariq
text: Sure... what?

speaker: claude
text: I am reporting it. Your live payment webhook key expired in August.
